segments.text: Forget everything [clears throat] your teacher told you. We are not learning English today. We are learning the native flow.
But wait, in school they taught you grammar rules and difficult vocabulary lists.
That is the old way.
That is why you feel stuck.
Here is the twist.
What if I told you that you can speak English naturally in just 21 days without memorizing anything?
I have a friend, Min.
He could barely say hello. He was just like you.
After 21 days, he was having real conversations. He understood movies. He felt confident.
So, how did he do it?
Simple.
We focus on how to sound like a native, not just read like a student.
Let's go.
This is your road map.
Let me tell you a secret.
Nobody talks about this.
Point one, stop studying, start listening.
You know, when you were a baby, you didn't study grammar, right?
You just listened.
Your brain copied the sounds.
You did it naturally.
So, for the next 21 days, do not study English.
Just consume it.
Find a podcast, a song, or a TV show.
It doesn't matter if you don't understand every word, just listen.
Listen to the rhythm.
Listen to the melody of the voice.
Your brain is like a sponge.
It will start to remember the patterns.
That was easy.
But point two is where we change the game completely.
Point two, steal the sound.
Here is the real secret. Many learners don't do this.
It's about the music of English, not just the words.
When you listen, pick one sentence, just one.
Play it again and again.
Now, say it out loud.
Do not try to be perfect.
Try to copy exactly how the speaker says it.
Do they make some sounds longer?
Do they make some sounds shorter?
Listen to how the words connect.
For example, they don't say, "I am going to." They say, "I'm going to."
This is how people really talk.
You are not learning words, you are stealing the sound.
You're probably thinking, "But what if I make a mistake?"
That is okay.
We need to talk about that next.
Point three, speak badly, but speak often.
Here's the problem with school.
They want you to be perfect. They make you afraid of mistakes.
This is terrible.
In the real world, communication is more important than perfection.
For 21 days, you must speak.
Even if it sounds bad.
Even if you use the wrong words.
Open your mouth.
Talk to yourself. Talk to a dog. Talk to a mirror.
I don't care if you say, "I go store yesterday."
The native will understand you. They will appreciate that you are trying.
[snorts]
The more you do this, the more you practice the sound.
Your mouth gets used to the movement.
It becomes easier.
I promise.
This is great, but guess what? There is one final step.
The most important secret to making it all stick.
Point four, the five-minute shadow.
Okay, this
is the biggest secret of all. This is the magic trick.
Are you ready?
Every morning, for just 5 minutes, do shadowing.
This is simple.
Take an audio clip of a native speaker. Put on your headphones.
Play it.
At the exact same time, try to speak along with them.
Don't pause. Just follow them.
It feels crazy. It feels fast.
At first, you can't keep up.
But after a few days, something amazing happens.
Your brain and your mouth start to work together.
You are learning to think in English.
Remember Min?
He did this for 21 days.
After 1 week, he could already follow faster sentences.
After 3 weeks, he was talking like a new person.
He didn't learn rules.
He learned the flow.
So, there you have it.
We are not learning English like a boring school subject.
We are learning to feel the rhythm, steal the sound, and speak without fear.
That is your 21-day plan.
It is simple.
It is effective.
It is the native flow.
Now, go and listen.
Steal the sound.
Shadow in the morning.
